questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a country that was culturally different from Denmark, but not too far away, so friends and family could visit. Italy's culture, food, outgoing and chill approach and especially the beautiful country and cities were crucial for my choice of destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really really recommend going to Italy. It is the most beautiful, charming and amazing country. There is much to see and experience in Milan, and the city has a great size - there is much to do in 5 months, but you still get the feeling that you know your way around the city after a while, and you can walk from one end of the city to the other in like an hour or so. Very charming even though it has a bad rep to a lot of people - there are so many charming areas that give you that authentic Italian experience, and also more modern areas, a very interesting combination. Sooo many good restaurants and bars, the university is beautiful, and it is a lively and fun city. I loved it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say that it is a stressful process figuring out everything, and it is very confusing as you do not always know who to contact with the different issues you face. But it is very much worth all the trouble.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had to check in at the International mobility office where Massimo Costa helped us sign our proof of attendance paper. We also received some emails along the way to inform us about practical things from Massimo. He was quick to reply to emails and helpful. There was also a group of volunteer students part of ESN that arranged a bunch of activities throughout the semester for Erasmus students to participate in and get to know each other. I did not go to any of them, but I think other people did. They had a big meeting in the beginning where they introduced us to all kinds of practical things about Milan, the university etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was a very stressful process. It is difficult to find apartments in Milan and it is just as expensive as in Copenhagen. We found ours through
housinganywhere.it
. You can also check
immobilaire.it
. We found ours through a private agency called Target apartments with a guy named Igor. He has many apartments around Milan and rents them out for a living, so he has his own company. Our experiences with him and his agency were good, and they were helpful and trustworthy. Slow in responding to us during the stay, but we eventually figured out that it is just the Italian way, they are chill and easy going and never get stressed, so you just need to patient which can be hard because they are so slow with everything and don't follow deadlines or time schedules in general. But be careful when looking for your own place, there are many people who try to scam exchange students. I have not heard of anyone who were scammed, but it's a general thing that they do it. But look for apartments early, almost right when you are granted a spot, and then you will be fine, because it does take time, and there are many exchange students in Milan, so you need to be fast. But the metro system is easy to use, so it's okay to not live in the center, I lived in the north of Milan, which was absolutely fine.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I haven't heard of anyone living on campus, I don't think there are many available rooms, so I would recommend checking out the facebook group for people going to Milan, people often look for a roomie on there if they have an extra room or something like that. And also, you can save a lot of money and live in something much nicer and bigger if you do not look for apartments right in the center of the city. This worked fine for us, because we lived close to a metro and they are easy to use and cover all of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not enough rooms available and they looked old

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
This was a confusing process I must say. It was difficult to navigate the website of unimi, and even finding the course catalogue was difficult. Here is a link to the course catalogue, hope that helps:
https://www.unimi.it/en/education/degree-programme-courses/degree-courses-2025-2026
Remember to change the year. You just click on Subject Area and look at the ones in capitol letters, otherwise it might not show any results. Be aware that the courses with no professor name are probably not offered. Some courses are both available with 6 and 9 ECTS, and I took journalism, media and politics with 9 ECTS, which meant that I took the same class as the ones who took it with 6 ECTS, but then I also had one more class once a week of 3 ECTS where the professor just added more in depth knowledge about the course, so that was basically the only difference. You will be changing your pre-approval of courses a couple of times as you do not know what courses will actually be offered until you get down there. And also, there is a week in september, the first week of school (around the 15th of september) where you can try many of the different courses you are interested in. There is no real lectures the first week of school, because students just shuffle around the courses to see which ones they want to take, and the professors just introduce the courses and talk about the exam methods and what the course is about, so you can just figure it all out when you get down there and also see what combination of courses would make a good schedule for you. I only took master's courses even though I'm on my bachelor's because there were almost no sociology courses available for bachelor's, but it was no issue at all, the courses were very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You make a pre-approval before coming to Milan to show UCPH that there are in fact relevant courses to take, and then you make a new one when you actually choose your courses in Milan and send that home again and then fill out your online learning agreement. So you also need to change your OLA once you have your actual courses figured out. 
When applying for the pre-approval they ask for a course code and that is just the combination of letters and numbers when you click on the course, e.g. Global Social Dynamics has the code SSD SPS/07. When you click on the course, there is a button at the right called Lessons timetable that you can click on and then you can combine different courses you want to take to see what your schedule would look like, that is very helpful when trying to figure out what courses to take and what schedule would work for you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not really any help honestly

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not all the classes I had looked at in the spring were actually available when I came to Milan in september, but I figured it out and chose other courses that were also relevant.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If "Value change and global societies" with professor Biolcati Rinaldi Ferruccio is available, I would really recommend it. He is an amazing professor, so good at explaining complex phenomena in an understandable way, and he is super nice and friendly. I would not take Global Social Dynamics with professor Triventi, it was like a crash course in sociology and just waaaayyyy to much information with 150 slides sometimes. He never had time to go through all of it, and it was just too much info about stuff that was so so so irrelevant. Do NOT recommend.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level is very low in general, I only had master's courses and it was very easy to get good grades. The courses I could take were quite similar, all about globalization and global societies etc, but they were okay. There are many presentations in class in general from the students, and every professor chooses his/her own exam method. So there is no standardization when it comes to exams, some classes you have to turn in a paper, do a presentation and do a written exam with 1-3 open questions that you have to answer without any notes - on paper with a pencil, very old fashioned. In other classes you can choose between different exam methods, either you can write a long paper, do open questions in one hour without notes or something third. It is a strange way to do exams, and basically just tests how well you remember the curricula. I thought it was a weird way to do exams in a subject like sociology because you don't really learn how to use the theories and methods, but only how to account for them. Some exams are multiple questions and then some open questions, but the open questions are not really open as they are "what is social control theory?" or "what characterizes globalization?" Yes, they are that simple and not open at all.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very easy as I explained. If you just show up to class and study for the exams, you will be fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The professors are definitely bright and knowledgable, but many courses are very low level and basically just rote learning. But I found most of them interesting.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Value change and global societies (recommend!) 
Global Social Dynamics (do not recommend) 
Globalization and cultural diversity (similar topics as in Sociologiske teoriudviklinger in Copenhagen, so it was an advantage for me that I had already had this course at home) 
Journalism, media and politics (it was okay but very common knowledge I feel like. We were examined only on the basis of a book we should read, the "open" questions were only based on this book)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Value change and global societies had very interesting topics such as immigration and immigrants' attitudes towards other immigrants, how they gradually assimilated to the opinions of the natives etc. It was basically about values and why values change in societies and what mechanisms cause this change, and then we looked at different aspects of values so values and attitudes towards immigrants, climate, gender roles, homosexuality, religion and secularization. GREAT course!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out to eat is not so cheap as you would expect from Italy, but alcohol and coffee is much cheaper. And all the Italian groceries are cheap, but other groceries are like Danish. Public transportation is very cheap if you download the ATM app and buy a student pass for 4-5 months, it's like 88 euros which is like 165 kr. per month and then you can travel all you want with metro and tram.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Fitness membership is SO EXPENSIVE!!! Like 700 kr. at least each month, so I ended up running instead because I could not afford fitness. I checked out almost all the fitness chains they had, and everywhere was super expensive even though the quality was low at most of them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN arranged activities like tennis matches, football etc but I did not participate in any

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Running maybe, there are many good parks to run in

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the train to other cities outside Milan such as Parma (!!!), Lake como in the summer, Bergamo, Firenze, Bologna etc. There is a pretty good railway system from Milan to many cities, so it is pretty easy to travel around. Can be expensive sometimes but it is also possible to find cheaper tickets.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, the Italians are very outgoing and when going out people love to talk to you when they notice you are not from Italy. They are very curious and proud of their country and love to talk about it and where they come from in Italy. The food is amazing, the attitude is laid back and easy going. This can also be a challenge though, because they never meet deadlines, they are often late and don't respond to messages and do not get things done which can be so very frustrating. The public transportation workers often strike because of bad conditions and salary, so I think we tried at least 10 times in the 5 months in Milan that the metro did not drive because of strikes. And then it is impossible to get around, because the busses often do not show up.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly talked to other exchange students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As I said before, the Italian way of doing things which is slow and the exact opposite of the Danish way. I really missed UCPH's way of doing and organizing things.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the passionate people, who love their country, going to football matches in San Siro, the way they really know how to make even the most random places cozy - they are even better at "hygge" than we are in Denmark. They have the most amazing and beautiful restaurants, both modern and also old fashioned, traditional and authentic. They hang out in the streets all year long where they drink their wine standing on the side walk in front of the bars if there is not room inside the bars, even in december and january. The food culture is just amazing, they love their food, and the way they are so traditional and rigid about it is amazing. They are a nice people who really have certain norms, like not drinking cappuccino after 12 o clock, and they will laugh at you if you order it after 12... They dress to impress, and they always greet each other politely.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have patience in Italy! Eat your way through the country. Relax, it will all work out, they don't stress so you don't have to either. They are helpful and they know that Erasmus students are also there to enjoy Italy, so they are less strict with us. They are accommodating to Erasmus students and want to help us through the process.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
ESN offers a student card that you can buy for 100 kr. and this gives you access to the activities that they arrange, but it also gives you discount to Ryan Air which flies to Bergamo airport where you can easily take a bus to Milano Centrale, the central station, so I bought that and that way got cheap flight tickets back and forth. Fly to either Bergamo or Linate. From Bergamo there is a bus right outside the airport that takes you straight to the central station for 12 euros, and you just buy they tickets at the bus, don't buy them in advance. They drive all the time and there are many of them. Ryan Air only flies to Bergamo. If you go to Linate you can fly with easyjet e.g. and take the metro directly to the city within like 15 minutes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Coming to a country where the attitude towards everything is more relaxed, even though it is also stressful at times. And then seeing how much they just hang out everywhere in the most nice and cool bars and restaurants and cafés, they really know how to enjoy life. The charming city, the many experiences and nice people. You just experience a culture and city much better when living there for longer time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Also the laid back easy going attitude of the Italians, my patience was challenged I must say

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Please go to Italy!!!!

questions.answer: Yes
